payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_session.py::test_a_second_stop_files_every_pair_left_as_an_error_naming_the_runtime_error stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/cell/session.py. The claim was "When the fresh cell also stops, or cannot be entered, no further cell is entered. A pair the fresh cell answered before its own stop keeps its outcome and carries no `unasked` key. Every pair still unasked then reads outcome `error`, never `unproven`. The pairs still unasked include the pair whose witness ask or line read was running when the fresh cell stopped. Its summary replaces the one the witness gate or the line read wrote. Each such pair's `unasked` key holds the text of the runtime error that ended the fresh cell. Its summary is `the probe cell stopped before this edit's answer was recorded: ` followed by that text after a stop. After a failed entry it is `the probe cell could not be entered: ` followed by that text. A survivor whose second ask stopped the fresh cell keeps `survived` and its one finding, with no `unasked` key. The witness drives a stop of the fresh cell at a witness ask, after it answered one pair, at a survivor's line read and at a survivor's second ask. It also drives a stop followed by a fresh cell that cannot be entered, and two cells that cannot be entered. In the same calls a pair with no edit and a refused pair still read `unproven` with no `unasked` key. Every pair in a repo whose head declares no `tests` gate reads `unproven` with no `unasked` key, and no cell is entered.". Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_session.py::test_a_probe_cell_that_stops_is_entered_once_more_for_every_pair_left, and the criterion's witness did not fail.
